title: Token Axiom: compact cost annotator & export patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Design a compact, attachable "cost annotator" that surfaces token-level cost breakdowns and attribution inline with Redwood Console timelines and logs, plus a flexible export UX for analysts. Scope: 1) Compact inline UI that attaches to message/response rows (hover or expand) to reveal per-token and per-facet charge attribution; 2) A cost-export composer allowing CSV/Parquet templates, anonymization presets, and role-aware rateband annotations; 3) Pricing UI patterns describing how to apply tiered ratebands, discounts, and SKU splits to exported lines; 4) Accessibility and privacy defaults (mask raw prompts unless viewer has permission). Out of scope: backend accounting engine changes (billing calculations are assumed available via API endpoints).
acceptance_criteria: Compact annotator displays total tokens, input vs output split, model variant and per-token unit cost on hover/expand
Attribution tab shows top-3 contributing prompt fragments with attribution percentage and confidence heuristic
Export composer supports prebuilt templates (Audit CSV, Billing Ledger, Analysis Parquet) and custom column mapping
Anonymize toggle hides raw prompt text and replaces with hashed fragment identifiers for exports
Pricing pattern docs include example rateband application and how discounts cascade across SKUs
Design passes accessibility contrast and keyboard navigation checks
Design handoff includes annotated Figma frames and a short interaction spec for engineering (6 key interactions)
design_notes: We took inspiration from inline code-review annotations and bank statement line-item UIs to keep the annotator low-friction. Key principles: minimal vertical noise, immediate clarity for costs, and strong affordances for exporting. The annotator uses a condensed two-line summary (left: tokens/cost, right: model+variant) and an expansion panel with tabs: Breakdown, Attribution, Pricing Impact, and Export. Breakdown is a lightweight sparkline + token table; Attribution pairs tokens->intent-fragments using heuristics (prefix, role tags, and fallback sampling). Pricing Impact shows which ratebands applied and what the marginal delta would be if rerouted to an alternative model/quantization profile.
decisions: Compact by default: keep rows single-line; expansion on hover/click to preserve dashboard density
Attribution heuristic: sequence-prefix weighting with a configurable fallback sampling mode (trade-off: deterministic but sometimes noisy vs sampled but more accurate)
Exports: include both human-friendly CSV for audits and Parquet schema for analytics pipelines
Anonymization default: ON for viewers without export permission (privacy-first posture)
Pricing sliders: show hypothetical toggles in 'Pricing Impact' but not apply them server-side; they are 'what-if' only unless user chooses 'apply to route' in a separate controls panel
reviews: PM feedback (Marco Nguyen 2026-03-04): prefer CSV audit rows to include 'route_id' and 'model_hash' columns by default
Eng feedback (Sofia Kim 2026-03-05): need API contract for anonymized fragments and sample-based attribution endpoint; recommended optimistic UI for expansion while backend resolves details
Security review (Ethan Clarke 2026-03-07): require export audit logs to be recorded in activity stream and gating by 'export' permission
Design critique (Riley Morgan 2026-03-10): iterate on token-sparkline color choices to work for deuteranopia; reduce micro-interaction duration from 240ms to 160ms
